news.headline: Super Micro Computer Reports Q4 After Close; Revenue Misses, EPS Ahead of Estimates
news.body: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) reported fiscal Q4 2026 results after the close on August 11, with EPS coming in ahead of consensus estimates but revenue falling short of the ~$11.56 billion analyst forecast — consistent with the company's July 21 preliminary update flagging revenue near the low end of the $11.0–$12.5 billion guidance range. The preliminary update had already flagged a gross margin beat of 15–17% versus prior guidance of 8.2–8.4%, driven by favorable customer and product mix, and a record backlog exceeding $60 billion. Options markets had priced in a 16–19% post-earnings price swing given the stock's binary reaction history. The results are closely watched as a bellwether for AI server infrastructure demand, with 101% year-over-year revenue growth expected for the quarter.

news.headline: Intel Launches Historic $15B Stock Offering to Fund AI & Foundry Expansion
news.body: Intel (INTC) announced a $15 billion underwritten public offering of common stock on August 10 — its first public share sale since its 1971 IPO listing — to fund capital expenditures and working capital amid an AI-driven demand surge. The company cited unprecedented customer demand for AI compute and flagged physical AI, advanced packaging, and external wafers as growth opportunities; 2026 capex guidance was recently raised above $20 billion. Shares initially slipped on dilution concerns before recovering toward $100, as INTC has nearly tripled year-to-date. The massive raise underscores the capital intensity of Intel's foundry turnaround strategy and its ambition to compete with TSMC in advanced chip manufacturing.

news.headline: Monday.com Drops ~10% as Weak Q3 Guidance Overshadows Q2 Earnings Beat
news.body: Monday.com (MNDY) reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.48, beating the $1.11 consensus by 33%, with revenue up 22% year-over-year to $364.6 million versus expectations of $355.5 million; AI ARR doubled quarter-over-quarter and now represents 17% of net new ARR. However, shares fell roughly 9–10% after the company guided Q3 revenue to $368–$370 million, below the $372.8 million analyst consensus, and announced a 20% workforce reduction as part of a restructuring to reinvest in AI. The guidance shortfall and layoff announcement overshadowed the strong beat and record adjusted operating income of $61.1 million. Markets are focused on whether the organizational transition will sustain the company's AI growth momentum.

news.headline: MarineMax Surges 45%+ on $1.5B Blackstone All-Cash Buyout at 96% Premium
news.body: MarineMax (NYSE: HZO) jumped over 45% to a 52-week high after announcing a definitive agreement to be acquired by Safe Harbor Marinas, a Blackstone Infrastructure portfolio company, for $53.00 per share in cash — an enterprise value of approximately $1.5 billion. The offer represents a 96% premium to HZO's January 30 undisturbed closing price of $27.03 and a 110% premium to the 90-day volume-weighted average price. The all-cash deal, unanimously approved by MarineMax's board, is expected to close by year-end 2026 pending shareholder and regulatory approval. The takeout price drives the stock's revaluation to deal-arbitrage dynamics rather than underlying boat retail fundamentals.

news.headline: GameStop Weighs Pulling $56B eBay Bid, Pivots Toward Partnership or JV
news.body: Bloomberg reported on August 10 that GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is considering withdrawing the company's $56 billion unsolicited takeover bid for eBay and may instead propose a partnership or joint venture leveraging GameStop's roughly 1,600 U.S. retail locations in high-margin categories such as trading cards and collectibles. eBay (EBAY) fell ~4% on the news while GME was also under pressure, as the shift signals Cohen may be backing away from a deal eBay's board had already rejected as 'neither credible nor attractive.' GameStop, holding a 9.75% stake in eBay, would seek board representation as part of any partnership arrangement. The development adds uncertainty to both stocks following GME's 28% decline since the original offer was floated in May.

news.headline: Tencent Music Reports Q2 2026 Earnings; Consensus Eyes $1.30B Revenue Beat Ahead of Tencent Parent Results
news.body: Tencent Music Entertainment Group (NYSE: TME; HKEX: 1698) released its unaudited Q2 2026 results on August 11 before the US market open, with analysts forecasting earnings of $0.24 per share on revenue of approximately $1.30 billion, up sharply from $1.15 billion in Q1. The report arrives one day ahead of parent Tencent Holdings' own Q2 2026 results — due after Hong Kong market close on August 12 — where gaming revenue deceleration and AI capital expenditure are the key focal points for investors. TME's prior quarter showed a net margin of 26.45% and return on equity of 11.2%, and recent earnings announcements have been followed by consistently positive next-day price moves on the Hong Kong bourse. The dual reporting window is being treated by the market as a two-day sentiment test for China's broader internet sector.

news.headline: CXMT Joins MSCI China All Shares Index via Fast-Track, Cementing Top-Market-Cap Status
news.body: ChangXin Memory Technologies (688825.SS), China's leading DRAM chipmaker, was officially added to the MSCI China All Shares Index on August 10 under MSCI's mega-IPO fast-track rule — just two weeks after its record-breaking STAR Market debut. MSCI waived its standard 15% free-float requirement, adding the stock at a free float of just 6.7%, making CXMT the second-largest constituent behind Tencent. The company swung from accumulated losses of 36.65 billion yuan through end-2025 to an expected first-half net profit of 50–57 billion yuan, with analysts forecasting full-year profit exceeding 120 billion yuan. The inclusion triggers mandatory passive buying from global index-tracking funds, strengthening foreign institutional inflows into China's AI-driven memory chip supply chain.

news.headline: Seoul Launches $3.5B Semiconductor Fund; KOSPI Sidecar Triggered on Volatile Session
news.body: South Korea's government announced a 5 trillion won ($3.52 billion) semiconductor fund on August 10 targeting chip materials, components, and fabless companies, plus an additional 5 trillion won in trade finance for suppliers—part of President Lee Jae-myung's broader $576 billion mega-project initiative involving Samsung and SK Hynix. KOSPI surged over 2% in morning trade, prompting a KOSDAQ Sidecar suspension of program buy orders, before paring gains to close up just 0.65% as semiconductor heavyweights SK Hynix (-0.14%) and Samsung Electronics (-0.43%) ended lower. On August 11, the KOSPI opened down 0.83% with SK Hynix falling over 2% as weak U.S. tech sentiment offset the policy boost. The fund and Mega Special Zone Act, if passed, would directly benefit domestic chip materials and equipment names.

news.headline: Unitree Robotics Shanghai IPO Draws 8,288x Oversubscription in Record Debut
news.body: Chinese humanoid robot maker Unitree Robotics (Yushu Technology) reported on August 10 that its STAR Market IPO was oversubscribed 8,288 times by retail investors, with 9.78 million accounts submitting valid applications for 53.6 billion shares against 40.45 million on offer. The final lot-winning rate fell to just 0.018%, raising 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) at 150.8 yuan per share and valuing the company at ~61 billion yuan. Unitree becomes China's first mainland-listed pure-play humanoid robot maker, setting a benchmark valuation of 219x 2025 earnings and 36x sales. The listing is expected to re-price the broader robotics sector on Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges ahead of its debut later this month.

news.headline: Nikkei 225 Climbs 2.08% to 66,970 on US Jobs Miss; AI Chip Stocks Lead Gains
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed up 2.08% at 66,970 on August 10, reaching multi-week highs after July U.S. nonfarm payrolls fell 23,000—badly missing the +80,000 consensus—reducing expectations for a near-term Fed rate hike. Chipmakers and AI-linked stocks led gains: Fujikura +7.6%, Advantest +6.4%, Tokyo Electron +4.1%, and Ibiden +4.0%. Japan's markets are closed on August 11 for Mountain Day, a public holiday. The Nikkei and KOSPI have moved in the same direction on 85% of trading days in 2026, reflecting overseas investors treating both markets as a unified AI/semiconductor trade.

news.headline: EIA August STEO Due Today; Hormuz Reopening Timeline Key Variable for Oil Outlook
news.body: The EIA's August 11 Short-Term Energy Outlook—the first since the July 7 edition that assumed the June US-Iran MOU would reopen the Strait of Hormuz—is released against a dramatically changed backdrop: renewed tanker attacks, stalled Oman-Iran negotiations, and Iran's hardened reopening conditions have pushed Brent back above $87/bbl versus the July STEO's $74/bbl Q3 forecast. The prior STEO expected most Gulf oil production to return to pre-conflict averages by year-end, but ongoing supply disruptions are deepening inventory draws estimated at 2.2 million b/d in Q3. Markets will scrutinize any revision to production recovery timelines and price forecasts.

news.headline: USDA August 12 WASDE Looms as First Survey-Based Corn/Soy Yield; Wheat Crop Near 56-Year Low
news.body: Grain markets are positioned ahead of tomorrow's August 12 WASDE—the first to incorporate field-survey-based yield estimates for corn and soybeans, replacing trend-line projections and historically the single largest price-moving USDA report of the crop year. US wheat production for 2026/27 is already tracking at 1.536 billion bushels, the lowest since 1970/71, with winter wheat down 29% year-on-year to 990 million bushels and Hard Red Winter set for its smallest crop since 1957/58. Ending stocks are projected 22% below last year. Corn yield uncertainty is elevated after above-normal July heat across the Northern Plains and western Corn Belt, with any downward yield revision potentially compounding already-tight global grain balances.

news.headline: Iran Strikes ADNOC Tanker in Hormuz; Houthis Hit Saudi Aramco Jazan Refinery
news.body: Iran's IRGC struck an ADNOC-operated tanker with a missile in the Strait of Hormuz on Aug. 8, while Houthi rebels launched a drone attack on Saudi Aramco's 400,000 bpd Jazan refinery on Aug. 9, triggering a fire that Saudi authorities said was extinguished without casualties. The dual strikes compound the Hormuz impasse: Iran's Supreme National Security Council declared the strait will not reopen until Washington 'corrects its behavior,' rejecting direct talks. Brent surged past $87/bbl on Aug. 10, extending a 5%-plus gain over the prior three sessions as the market priced in sustained supply disruption risk. The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen below 300 million barrels—its lowest since 1983—leaving diminishing buffer against further escalation.

news.headline: Gold Tops $4,378 on Monday After 7% Weekly Surge Driven by NFP Shock
news.body: Gold held above $4,378/oz on Aug. 10, consolidating a weekly gain of more than 7%—its best week since January—after the BLS reported the US economy shed 23,000 nonfarm payroll jobs in July, a severe miss versus the 80,000 consensus, marking the second labor market contraction of 2026. Prior-month revisions erased an additional 103,000 jobs combined for May and June. The weak data collapsed Fed rate-hike odds for September to ~55% from 63% the prior week and dragged Treasury yields lower, reducing the opportunity cost of holding bullion. Chinese institutional investors continued adding to gold-backed long positions, and central bank buying remained a structural tailwind.

news.headline: China July Copper Imports Jump 9.1% YoY to 480kt, Reversing H1 Tariff Drag
news.body: China's preliminary customs data released Aug. 8 showed unwrought copper imports rose 9.1% year-on-year and 4.3% month-on-month to 480,000 tonnes in July, the strongest monthly reading in 2026, as domestic demand recovered after Trump dropped plans for a 50% tariff on refined copper. Copper concentrate imports surged 18% YoY to 2.6 million tonnes, reflecting robust domestic refining output. Cumulative imports remain down 2.7% YoY through July as H1 supply was diverted to US warehouses ahead of tariff risk. The data supported copper futures, which have climbed for a fourth consecutive week, with COMEX speculative longs rising to their highest in months.
